newsitem.title: UK: UK's Oftel set to reject BT plan on schools.
newsitem.headline: UK's Oftel set to reject BT plan on schools.

text.p: The UK's Oftel watchdog is set to reject proposals from British Telecommunications Plc to offer schools access to the information superhighway, its head said on Thursday.
Oftel Director General Don Cruickshank told reporters BT's interim plans promoted access via its own Internet service provider, effectively locking out most rivals.
"It is difficult to see how this is of interest to schools," Cruickshank said at a press briefing, adding Oftel's formal response was likely to be published in the next couple of days.
Industry analysts have said acceptance of the proposals could help BT win an early release from a ban on using its extensive network for potentially lucrative entertainment services.
However, Cruickshank said the two issues were unrelated. "This schools issue is being pursued independently," he said.

Cruickshank said BT had taken six months to come up with its proposals. It had finally proposed an interim solution to allow schools to go online when the new academic year starts in September plus longer-term plans.
Further consultation is set to follow, delaying the introduction of BT services to schools beyond September. A BT spokeswoman said the company would be disappointed if Oftel rejected its proposals.
"We came up with specific new packages for the autumn to try to meet what schools were asking for. We felt it was a constructive way forward," she said.
BT said access to its service providers was only via BT numbers but added that there was a range of alternatives for schools to select.
Oftel has already approved cable company plans to allow schools access to the Internet and some 600-800 schools have signed up under the cable scheme.
Cruickshank said schools wanted to be able to link groups of 10-20 to the Internet at affordable and predictable prices.
